format: Speaking Q11 意見を述べる
question: Some people prefer to work for a large company, while others prefer to work for a small company. Which do you prefer and why? Give reasons or examples to support your opinion.
answer: I prefer to work for a small company, for two main reasons. First, in a small company, each employee has more responsibility. I could be involved in many different projects, so I would learn new skills quickly. Second, it's easier to communicate with everyone, including the managers. For example, my friend works at a small design firm, and she can share her ideas directly with the president. Her suggestions are often used, and she feels that her work really matters. Of course, large companies may offer higher salaries and more stability, but for me, personal growth is more important. That's why I would choose a small company.
explanation: 立場→理由1→理由2＋具体例→反対意見への言及→結論、の流れで60秒話す。 準備45秒・解答60秒想定。

format: Speaking Q11 意見を述べる
question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? "Employees should be allowed to wear casual clothes at work." Give reasons or examples to support your opinion.
answer: I agree that employees should be allowed to wear casual clothes at work. First, people feel more comfortable in casual clothes, and when they are comfortable, they can concentrate better on their work. Second, casual clothes can save employees money, because suits and formal shoes are expensive. For example, at my company, we started a casual dress policy last year, and many people said they felt more relaxed and creative. However, I think employees should still dress formally when they meet clients. Overall, a casual dress policy is a good idea for most workplaces.
explanation: 賛否を最初に明言し、理由2つと自社の例、条件付きの例外を述べる。 準備45秒・解答60秒想定。

format: Speaking Q11 意見を述べる
question: What is the most important quality for a team leader to have? Give reasons or examples to support your opinion.
answer: In my opinion, the most important quality for a team leader is good communication. A leader has to explain goals clearly so that everyone knows what to do. If the instructions are unclear, team members may waste time or make mistakes. A good communicator also listens carefully. For example, my previous manager held short meetings every Monday and always asked for our opinions. Because of this, problems were solved early, and we trusted her. Other qualities, like experience and technical knowledge, are also useful, but without communication, a team cannot work well together. So I believe communication is the key quality.
explanation: 1つの資質に絞り、理由→具体例→他の資質との比較→結論で深める。 準備45秒・解答60秒想定。

format: Speaking Q11 意見を述べる
question: Some people think it is better to take one long vacation each year. Others prefer to take several short vacations. Which do you prefer and why?
answer: I prefer to take several short vacations during the year. The main reason is that short breaks help me stay refreshed all year long. If I take only one long vacation, I feel tired for many months before it. Also, short trips are easier to plan, and it's easier for my coworkers to cover my work for a few days than for two weeks. For example, last year I took three long weekends, and each time I came back to work with more energy. For these reasons, I think several short vacations are better for me.

format: Speaking Q11 意見を述べる
question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? "Companies should provide training programs for their employees even if the training is expensive." Give reasons or examples to support your opinion.
answer: I strongly agree with this statement. First, training helps employees improve their skills, and this directly benefits the company through better products and services. Second, when companies invest in their staff, employees feel valued, so they are more likely to stay with the company. Replacing workers who leave is often more expensive than training them. For instance, my company pays for English lessons, and several colleagues have since been able to work with overseas clients. Although training costs money in the short term, it is a smart investment in the long term.
explanation: 短期のコストと長期の利益を対比させると説得力が増す。 準備45秒・解答60秒想定。

format: Speaking Q11 意見を述べる
question: Which is the best way to learn about a new job: reading a manual, watching an experienced coworker, or attending a training session? Give reasons or examples to support your opinion.
answer: I think the best way to learn about a new job is by watching an experienced coworker. When I watch someone do the job, I can see the real steps, including small tips that are not written in a manual. I can also ask questions right away. For example, when I started my job at a hotel, I followed a senior receptionist for a week. I learned how to deal with difficult guests just by watching her. Manuals and training sessions are helpful, but they can't show every real situation. So watching a coworker is the most effective way.
explanation: 3択の問題では1つを選び、他の2つが劣る理由にも短く触れる。 準備45秒・解答60秒想定。

format: Speaking Q11 意見を述べる
question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? "In the future, most meetings will be held online rather than in person." Give reasons or examples to support your opinion.
answer: I partly agree with this statement. On the one hand, online meetings save a lot of time and money, because nobody has to travel. They also make it easy to include people from different cities or countries. My team already holds most of our weekly meetings online. On the other hand, some meetings work better in person, such as first meetings with new clients or brainstorming sessions, where body language and casual conversation are important. So I think most routine meetings will move online, but important face-to-face meetings will not disappear completely.

format: Speaking Q11 意見を述べる
question: Some people think that a company's location is very important when choosing a job. Do you agree? Why or why not?
answer: Yes, I agree that location is very important. First, if the office is close to my home, I can save time and money on commuting. That gives me more time for my family and hobbies. Second, a short commute reduces stress. For example, I used to commute for ninety minutes each way, and I was always tired. After I changed jobs, my commute became twenty minutes, and I feel much healthier. Salary and the type of work also matter, of course, but location has a big effect on daily life. That's why I think it's very important.
